title: Kth Smallest in a Two-Way Sorted Grid
statement:
You get an n × n grid where every row is sorted in non-decreasing order from left to right, and every column is sorted in non-decreasing order from top to bottom.

Return the k-th smallest value in the whole grid, counting duplicates separately (so it is the value at position k if you listed all n² values in sorted order, starting at 1).

Aim for less memory than O(n²).

examples.why: Sorted: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, … The fourth value is in the middle row; reading row by row would give 7.
Duplicates count separately: 2, 2, 2, 3. Counting distinct values would give 3.
One cell, and it may be negative.

hints: Listing and sorting all n² values works. What does the sorted structure of the grid let you skip?
Pick a value x. Starting from the bottom-left corner, you can count how many cells are ≤ x in O(n) by walking up and right, like a staircase.
That count only grows as x grows. Binary search on the value: find the smallest x whose count is at least k. That x is always a grid value.

explain.intuition:
The grid is sorted in two directions but not globally, so you can't just index into it. You can, however, answer "how many cells are ≤ x?" fast. Start at the bottom-left. If that cell is ≤ x, every cell above it in the column is too, so add row + 1 and move right. Otherwise move up. Each step leaves a row or a column for good: O(n).

The count is monotone in x, so binary search over values. The smallest x with count(x) ≥ k is the answer, and it is always an actual cell value: if it weren't, a smaller x would give the same count. A min-heap that pops k times also works, at O(k log n).
steps: While lo < hi: let mid be the floor of the midpoint and count cells ≤ mid with the staircase walk.
If the count is less than k, set lo = mid + 1; otherwise hi = mid.
pitfalls: Assuming the last cell of a row is smaller than the first cell of the next row. Only rows and columns are sorted; reading row by row gives 7 in the first example.
Counting distinct values. Duplicates take separate positions.
Computing the midpoint as (lo + hi) / 2 with truncation toward zero. With negative values it rounds the wrong way and the loop never ends; use floor.

complexity.time: O(n log R), R = value range

solutions.title: Flatten and sort
solutions.idea: Copy every value into one list, sort it and read position k − 1.

solutions.title: Min-heap over the rows
solutions.idea: Start with the first cell of each row in a heap. Pop the smallest k − 1 times, each time pushing the next cell of the same row.

solutions.title: Binary search on the value
solutions.idea: Count cells ≤ x with a staircase walk from the bottom-left corner, and binary search for the smallest x whose count reaches k.
